items.title: 18.7.1 Ligand Exchange Reactions of Copper(II) Complexes

source_refs.note: Topic 18.7.1 with Figures 18.7 and 18.8, printed page 25.

blocks.text: Whenever, we write Cu²⁺(aq), we actually refer to the complex ion [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺. This ion gives blue colour to the solution of a copper(II) salt, for example, copper sulphate. On adding sodium hydroxide to a copper(II) solution, a light blue precipitate is formed. Two water ligands are replaced by two hydroxide ions in this reaction.
If concentrated ammonia solution is added, the light blue precipitate dissolves resulting in a dark blue solution.
The structure of [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺(aq) is shown in Figure 18.7. Water ligands in [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ can also be exchanged directly with ammonia by replacing four water molecules.
For simplicity, [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ is usually written as [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺.

blocks.alt: [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ in square brackets: Cu in the centre with four NH3 at the corners of a dashed square plane (the front two on wedge bonds, the back two on dashed bonds) and one H2O above and one below the plane.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.7: Structure of [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺(aq) ion (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.7).

blocks.text: The chloride ions can also replace water ligands in [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ on addition of concentrated hydrochloric acid drop by drop. A yellow solution is obtained that contains the complex ion [CuCl₄]²⁻ (Figure 18.8).

blocks.alt: Three flasks. Middle ('Start here'): blue [Cu(H2O)6]2+, the well-known blue Cu2+ complex with water. Left, beside a conc. HCl bottle: yellow-green [CuCl4]2-, which forms on adding conc. HCl. Right, beside a conc. NH3 bottle: dark blue [Cu(H2O)2(NH3)4]2+, which forms on adding conc. NH3. Equilibrium arrows join the flasks.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.8: Colour changes as a result of ligand exchange reaction (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.8).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed caption text reads ‘This is yellow-green complex forms on adding conc. HCl.’; it should read ‘This yellow-green complex forms on adding conc. HCl.’
